title: More Nigerians Are Bringing Dogs Home — Here's How to Do It Safely
body:
More Nigerian households are opening their doors to dogs, and not just as guard animals patrolling a compound. The Guardian recently reported on how attitudes are shifting, with people now stopping in the street to ask a dog's name, or reaching over to stroke one, instead of crossing the road to avoid it.

That shift matters for how people actually find their next pet. As interest grows, so does the number of routes people use to connect: a friend's litter, a breeder found through a WhatsApp group, a listing shared around a neighborhood page. Most of these connections are perfectly ordinary. But rising interest in pets, anywhere in the world, tends to also draw people trying to take advantage of it: impersonation messages, requests for a "deposit" before a pet has even been seen, or pressure to send money because a pet supposedly needs to travel to reach you.

None of that fits how a real, local pet handoff actually works. The pattern worth remembering is simple: if you have not seen the pet and the person in front of you, and the conversation has turned to sending money first, something is wrong. A legitimate mating, adoption, or sale in Nigeria almost never involves shipping. You and the other owner are usually a short drive apart, not a courier delivery apart.

That reasoning is also why PetMatch works the way it does. It is a free directory, not a marketplace, so no payment, deposit, or fee of any kind passes through the platform itself. Listings are self-reported by the people who post them, not independently verified, so it is worth treating every one the way you would treat a stranger's word, right up until you have actually met them and their pet. Talk on WhatsApp first, meet somewhere neutral rather than heading straight to someone's home, and ask to see vaccination and health records before agreeing to anything.

None of this is meant to make dog or cat ownership sound risky. It is closer to the opposite: knowing what a normal, local match looks like is exactly what makes it easy to spot the version that isn't. More on meeting another owner safely is at https://petmatch.fit/safety.
link_label: The Guardian: Nigerians embrace dogs as pets
